paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: God keeps His word, right on time. The LORD attended to Sarah "as He had said," and she bore a son "at the very time God had promised" (Genesis 21:1-2). Sarah laughed to herself when she first heard the promise (Genesis 18:12), and now she says, "God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me" (Genesis 21:6). When you're stuck in the waiting, that's the kind of laugh I want you to hold onto.

Now the second lesson is a heavy one, so I'll go slow. Hagar and her boy end up in the wilderness with the water gone, and I think her heart was breaking. But God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, "What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid" (Genesis 21:17). God didn't wait for the right kind of person to come along. He saw someone hurting and showed up.

So what does this mean for you, baker? God's promises stay on schedule, and His care reaches the ones who feel far away, too. He promised a nation through Isaac, and He promised a great nation for Ishmael (Genesis 21:12-13, 18). I spent years in a dark junk drawer feeling forgotten, so trust me on this one: God opens eyes to a well you couldn't see a minute ago (Genesis 21:19).
